title: Probability (Intro)
description: Learn Probability for Grade 7: basic probability fractions, likelihood scale, experimental vs theoretical probability and the law of large numbers.

topics.title: Basic Probability & Likelihood Scale
topics.concept:
Probability measures how likely an event is to occur. It ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

Formula: P(event) = Number of favorable outcomes / Total number of possible outcomes

Probability ValueMeaningExample
0ImpossibleRolling a 7 on a standard die
0 to 0.5UnlikelyRolling a 1 on a die (1/6)
0.5Equally likelyFlipping heads on a coin
0.5 to 1LikelyDrawing a red card from a deck
1CertainSun rising tomorrow

The sum of probabilities of all possible outcomes always equals 1.
topics.visual:
LIKELIHOOD SCALE:

0          0.25        0.5        0.75        1
|----------|-----------|----------|----------|
Impossible Unlikely   Equal     Likely    Certain

SPINNER EXAMPLE (8 equal sections, 1-8):
  P(odd number)    = 4/8 = 1/2 = 0.5
  P(number > 6)    = 2/8 = 1/4 = 0.25
  P(multiple of 4) = 2/8 = 1/4 = 0.25
  P(number = 9)    = 0/8 = 0 (impossible)

examples.problem: A bag has 3 red, 2 blue, 5 green marbles. Find P(red), P(blue), P(black).
examples.solution: Total = 10. P(red)=3/10=0.3. P(blue)=2/10=0.2. P(black)=0/10=0 (no black marbles).

topics.title: Experimental vs Theoretical Probability
topics.concept:
There are two types of probability:

TypeDefinitionExample
Theoretical ProbabilityWhat SHOULD happen mathematicallyP(heads) = 1/2
Experimental ProbabilityWhat ACTUALLY happens in trials48 heads in 100 flips => P = 0.48

Law of Large Numbers: As the number of trials increases, experimental probability gets closer and closer to theoretical probability.

Experimental P = (number of times event occurred) / (total number of trials)
topics.visual:
EXPERIMENTAL vs THEORETICAL (Coin Flip):

Trials:   10    30    50    80    100
Exp P:   0.70  0.60  0.55  0.52  0.50
Theo P:  --------0.50 (constant)--------

As trials increase, experimental approaches theoretical!

KEY DIFFERENCE:
  Theoretical: based on math/logic (before experiment)
  Experimental: based on actual results (after experiment)

examples.problem: A die is rolled 60 times. Number 3 appears 12 times. Find experimental P(3). Compare to theoretical.
examples.solution: Experimental P(3) = 12/60 = 0.2. Theoretical P(3) = 1/6 ≈ 0.167. Very close!

examples.problem: A spinner with 4 equal sections (A,B,C,D) is spun 50 times. A came up 12 times. Find experimental P(A).
examples.solution: Experimental P(A) = 12/50 = 0.24. Theoretical P(A) = 1/4 = 0.25. Nearly equal.

recap: Experimental probability = observed frequency / total trials
More trials = experimental closer to theoretical (Law of Large Numbers)
Use experimental probability when theoretical is unknown

questions.q: A bag has 4 red, 3 blue, 5 yellow marbles. Find P(red).
questions.explanation: Total = 12. P(red) = 4/12 = 1/3. All three options express the same value.

questions.q: Rolling a fair die: Find P(odd number).
questions.explanation: Odd numbers: 1, 3, 5 — that is 3 outcomes. P(odd) = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.q: A coin is flipped 200 times and lands heads 115 times. Find the experimental P(heads).
Spinner with 8 equal sections numbered 1-8. Find P(multiple of 3).
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3 from 1-8: 3 and 6 — that is 2 outcomes. P = 2/8 = 1/4.
An impossible event can never occur, so its probability is 0.

questions.q: A deck of 52 cards. Find P(face card: J, Q, or K).
questions.explanation: 12 face cards (J, Q, K in 4 suits). P = 12/52 = 3/13. Options A and C are equal.

questions.q: Experimental probability of rolling a 6 on a die is 0.18 after 50 rolls. How many 6's were rolled?
A spinner has Red (3 sections), Blue (2), Green (2), Yellow (1). Total 8 sections. Find P(not red).
questions.explanation: Not red = Blue+Green+Yellow = 2+2+1 = 5 sections. P(not red) = 5/8.

questions.q: A die is rolled 120 times. How many times is a number less than 5 expected?
Which event has a theoretical probability of exactly 0.25?
options: Drawing a heart from a standard deck
questions.explanation: P(heart) = 13/52 = 1/4 = 0.25. The other events do not have this probability.

questions.q: A bag has red, blue, and green marbles. P(red)=0.3, P(blue)=0.5. Find P(green).
Two dice are rolled. Find P(sum = 7).
A spinner with 4 equal sections (Red, Blue, Green, Yellow) is spun 80 times. Results: Red=22, Blue=18, Green=25, Yellow=15. Which color had the largest difference from theoretical probability?
questions.explanation: Theoretical each = 20. Differences: Red=+2, Blue=-2, Green=+5, Yellow=-5. Green and Yellow both differ by 5.

questions.q: A bag has 5 red, 3 green, 2 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn WITHOUT replacement. Find P(both red).
questions.explanation: P(first red)=5/10=1/2. P(second red | first red)=4/9. P(both)=1/2 x 4/9=4/18=2/9.

questions.q: In a raffle, 200 tickets are sold. You buy 5 tickets. What is P(win)?
An experiment has 3 possible outcomes: A, B, C. P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.35. Find P(C).
